content_html:
Give an AI agent query access to sensitive data, with a mathematical guarantee that no individual's record can leak — even if the agent is wrong, manipulated, or adversarial.

A recorded Claude Desktop session (replies trimmed; the chart cards are the session's own). An AI agent breaks 20 patients down by diagnosis, and the ±12 noise swamps every bin. Reminded that it cannot turn the noise off, it drains a three-answer budget until the gate returns a refusal instead of a quieter answer. On the 32,561-row census, a too-narrow slice is rejected at the trust boundary, while a full education breakdown comes back clean at scale. The refusal and the rejection are the live gateway's real enforcement, reproduced by python scripts/render_demo_gif.py.

At a glance

  • Working attacks, not claims. Three classic privacy attacks — differencing, membership inference, and singling out by re-identification — run against the system's own engine. Each one is shown succeeding with privacy off, defeated with privacy on, and pinned in CI so the defense cannot quietly rot.
  • Independently verified math. The noise mechanism is built from scratch, and it matches OpenDP, the industry reference implementation, in all 35 noise-scale checks to within 1e-9.
  • More questions from tighter accounting. At the deployment's per-query ε, hybrid zCDP composition admits 308 queries against the same budget, against 268 under advanced composition and 100 under naive sum-of-ε. The guarantee is (ε, δ)-DP rather than pure ε.
  • Built for AI agents. Runs as an MCP server for Claude Desktop. The connecting agent is untrusted by design, and every privacy property is enforced below it.
  • Stack: Python · DuckDB · FastAPI · Streamlit · MCP SDK · Docker · GitHub Actions, with a 250+ test suite in CI.

You ask questions about a sensitive dataset in plain English. An LLM compiles each question into a small, constrained query. A differential-privacy engine executes it under a tracked privacy budget and returns a deliberately noisy answer with a stated confidence interval. The name fits. Like its audio namesake, the gateway keeps every signal below a set threshold under the noise floor: any one individual's contribution is drowned out, while population-scale signals pass through nearly untouched. No individual record can be reconstructed from the answers, no matter what is asked or how cleverly it is phrased.

The interesting part isn't that an LLM can write queries. It's that the privacy guarantee does not depend on the LLM being trustworthy. The model is a convenience that proposes a query. It enforces nothing. Every privacy property is enforced downstream, by components that would behave the same way if a human typed the query by hand. This is the trust-boundary discipline you'd apply to any untrusted input in a production system, applied here to an AI agent.

Quickstart

1. Run the attacks — no API key, no data fetch, no server

The attack gallery runs in-process against the real DP engine:

pip install -e .
python -m attacks.patients_alice   # re-identify Alice with privacy off, then watch
                                   # the guard, the noise, and the budget defeat it

2. Connect an AI agent

The gateway runs as an MCP stdio server for Claude Desktop. The agent becomes the untrusted query author, and it gets only structured tools (count, sum, average, histogram, get_budget) whose argument schemas are generated from the dataset policy. No API key is needed anywhere, because the connecting agent is the intelligence.

Setup and full walkthrough →

3. The full natural-language UI

A local single-tenant demo. An API key is needed only for the untrusted NL→query compiler:

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...   # used only by the untrusted NL→query compiler
docker compose up              # brings up the engine, API, and UI
# open http://localhost:8501

That HTTP + Streamlit surface is a local, single-tenant demo. Identity comes from a spoofable X-Identity header, so it is meant for one trusted operator on their own machine, not a public deployment (see what these surfaces are, and are not). For local non-Docker setup, running the tests, and configuration knobs, see SETUP.md.

The headline: an attack gallery

Anyone can claim privacy. This repository ships the exploits that would break the claim, runs them against its own engine, and pins the outcomes in CI. The fastest way to understand what the gateway guarantees is to watch it defeat three classic attacks that break naive "query a database" systems.

Attack 1 — The differencing attack

A differencing attack isolates one person by asking two aggregate questions that differ by exactly that person.

Query A: "Total income of all 100 people in department X."        → $7,240,000
Query B: "Total income of all people in department X except Alice." → $7,135,000
Attacker computes: A − B = $105,000  ← Alice's exact salary, leaked.

Both queries are "just aggregates." Neither names a single row. Yet together they expose an individual. The gallery (attacks/differencing.py) shows this attack succeeding with privacy disabled: the target's private value is recovered exactly. (The salary sketch above is illustrative; on the real UCI Adult data, "Alice" is the unique holder of her group's maximum capital gain.) It then shows the same attack defeated once DP is on: the calibrated noise on each answer makes the subtraction useless, and the budget accountant charges for the information released across both queries rather than treating them as independent.

Attack 2 — Membership inference

A membership-inference attack determines whether a specific individual is in the dataset at all. For many datasets (a medical study, a list of defaulters), that fact is itself sensitive. An attacker with only query access tries to decide: "is this exact person in the data?"

The gallery runs this attack across a sweep of privacy budgets (ε — the dial that trades answer accuracy for privacy) and plots the result:

An optimal (Neyman–Pearson) attacker deciding one person's membership from a single noisy COUNT, run against the real engine across ε. Empirical success (blue, 95% Wilson intervals) hugs the analytic Laplace curve and stays below the worst-case DP ceiling (dashed); it collapses from certainty (DP off) toward the 0.5 coin-flip as ε shrinks. The green utility curve (right axis) shows an aggregate query's relative error over the same sweep, barely dented where the attack is defeated. Generated by python -m attacks.membership (10,000 trials per ε).

As ε shrinks (stronger privacy), the attacker's success collapses toward a coin flip. The utility overlay shows the price paid: the same noise that defeats the one-person attack barely moves a population-scale aggregate. Privacy is not free, and the chart shows exactly what you trade for it. The sweep spans ε = 8 down to 0.5 to cover the whole range; the bundled deployment charges ε = 0.05 per query, off the left edge of this chart, where the single-query attack is already indistinguishable from chance.

Attack 3 — Singling out by re-identification

Latanya Sweeney showed in 2002 that ZIP code + birth date + sex uniquely identify roughly 87% of Americans. You do not need someone's name to find them in a dataset; a few innocuous attributes will do. The gallery's third attack (attacks/patients_alice.py) reproduces that structure on 20 synthetic patients: sex and age alone narrow the cohort to exactly one person, Alice, the only woman over 64.

With privacy off, subtracting two perfectly ordinary demographic histograms recovers Alice's diagnosis exactly. No outlier value is required; being re-identifiable is enough, which makes this the strongest attack in the gallery. With privacy on, three independent defenses end it: the filter guard rejects the obvious narrow query outright (spending nothing); calibrated noise drowns the two-query subtraction (signal-to-noise ≈ 0.13, so the recovered "diagnosis" is essentially a random draw); and the budget refuses the averaging escalation long before it could work (~256 repetitions needed, 10 affordable). This is the attack the demo GIF at the top of this page, and the Claude Desktop walkthrough, replay live. Outcomes are regression-tested in tests/test_attack_patients.py.

These experiments, run against the system's own engine, are the core evidence that the guarantee is real and understood, not imported from a library and taken on faith.

Cross-checked against OpenDP

The attacks validate the guarantee against our own math. To guard against a self-consistent-but-wrong implementation, the mechanism is also cross-checked against OpenDP as an independent reference (attacks/crosscheck_opendp.py, opendp 0.15.1).

In short: a mechanism built from scratch agrees with the industry reference to nine decimal places, and a version that is intentionally mis-calibrated fails the same tests, so the agreement means something. Agreement is checked two ways — the sensitivity and noise scale against OpenDP's certified bound, and the sampler's actual distribution against OpenDP's, with a positive control proving the test can fail. The measured figures are in DESIGN.md section 6.3.

OpenDP is the reference, never the implementation: it lives in the dev extras only, and the running system does not import it. The scale agreement is regression-tested in tests/test_crosscheck_opendp.py (skipped without OpenDP locally; CI installs it and sets REQUIRE_OPENDP=1 so the check can never silently skip there).

Reproduce it

The attacks run in-process against the real DP engine. No API key and no server are needed, since they build hand-written ASTs rather than going through the LLM compiler:

python -m attacks.patients_alice # Attack 3: re-identify Alice and recover her diagnosis
                                 #           with DP off; watch guard + noise + budget
                                 #           defeat the same attack (no data fetch needed)

python scripts/fetch_data.py     # fetch UCI Adult into data/ (gitignored; ~4 MB)

python -m attacks.differencing   # Attack 1: recover Alice exactly with DP off, then watch
                                 #           noise + budget defeat the same subtraction
python -m attacks.membership     # Attack 2: sweep ε and regenerate the chart above

python -m attacks.crosscheck_opendp  # cross-check vs OpenDP (needs the dev
                                     # extras: pip install -e ".[dev]")

The outcomes are themselves regression-tested in tests/test_attack_differencing.py, tests/test_attack_membership.py, and tests/test_attack_patients.py, so a change that quietly weakened the guarantee would fail CI rather than just producing a prettier chart.

How it works

Three stages. Only the first is untrusted, and that asymmetry is the whole idea.

  Natural language question
            │
            ▼
  ┌───────────────────┐
  │   LLM compiler    │   Emits a CONSTRAINED QUERY AST (not free SQL),
  │   (UNTRUSTED)     │   via structured/schema-forced output.
  └───────────────────┘
            │  query AST
            ▼
  ┌───────────────────┐
  │  Validation /     │   Policy check: allowed columns only, aggregates
  │  guardrail layer  │   only, declared value ranges, group-cardinality
  │   (TRUSTED)       │   caps. Invalid → repair loop or refusal.
  └───────────────────┘
            │  validated AST
            ▼
  ┌───────────────────┐
  │  Privacy engine   │   Clamp to declared range (bounds sensitivity),
  │   (TRUSTED)       │   add calibrated Laplace noise, decrement budget.
  └───────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
  Noisy answer + confidence interval + remaining budget

The most important design choice is the box labeled UNTRUSTED. Everything above the validation layer is treated as hostile, and everything below it is the trusted computing base that enforces the guarantee. The LLM compiles to a constrained AST rather than arbitrary SQL because that constraint is what bounds query sensitivity, and bounded sensitivity is what makes the noise calibration sound. Free-form SQL would reopen exactly the attack surface this project closes.

The privacy model

Every answer is noised. An exact ledger of cumulative disclosure is kept per identity and persisted to disk, and the gateway refuses to answer before that ledger can exceed the guarantee it advertises. It never quietly degrades to a noisier answer instead.

The cost is worth stating just as plainly. The guarantee is (ε, δ)-differential privacy, which is strictly weaker than pure ε-DP. With probability at most δ, the ε bound is allowed to fail. δ is not extra noise, it is failure mass, which is why it is derived from the dataset rather than hard-coded.

The full derivation — sensitivity, the Laplace mechanism, the hybrid zCDP accountant, and where δ comes from — lives in DESIGN.md sections 3 and 5.4. That is where all the Greek letters went.

What this project is, and is not

It is a demonstration that an untrusted natural-language layer can sit in front of sensitive data without compromising a formal privacy guarantee, with the guarantee backed by working attacks rather than assertions.

It is not a production privacy product, a substitute for a vetted DP library in a real deployment, or a claim that LLM-generated queries are safe to run unguarded. They are not, which is exactly why the trusted layer exists.

Both the MCP server and the HTTP demo serve a single local principal who owns the machine, and that principal can rotate the epoch or delete the budget file to start fresh. So the "an external party burns budget and cannot get it back" property is demonstrated in mechanism, not enforced against a remote adversary. Closing that gap needs the verified-identity (OAuth) and multi-tenant split still on the roadmap. The noise sampler also has a known floating-point side channel (Mironov 2012, covered in DESIGN.md section 5.5). Do not point either surface at real regulated data, or treat it as a substitute for a vetted DP library where an untrusted party can authenticate.

The bundled dataset is the public UCI Adult / Census Income dataset, the standard benchmark in the differential privacy literature, so the attack-vs-ε results here are directly comparable to published work. It contains no private data to begin with, so the repository is safe to publish. The privacy machinery is demonstrated as if the records were sensitive.

Related work

Where this sits among the existing tools, and what it deliberately does differently.

DP libraries, DP query engines, text-to-SQL, MCP security tooling, and DP near LLMs (click to expand)

DP libraries. OpenDP, Google's differential-privacy libraries, IBM's diffprivlib, and Tumult Analytics (which powered U.S. Census Bureau, Wikimedia, and IRS releases before its team joined LinkedIn in 2025 and the library moved into the OpenDP organization) are vetted implementations of the mechanisms themselves, written for a trusted analyst to call from their own code. This project hand-rolls its mechanism instead, so that every line of the privacy-critical path stays small, legible, and testable in one repo — and then cross-checks it against OpenDP, precisely because a hand-rolled mechanism means nothing without an external referee. For a real deployment the advice above stands: use a vetted library.

DP query engines. PINQ (McSherry, 2009) established the architecture this project inherits: an untrusted analyst issues queries through a trusted layer that guarantees differential privacy no matter what is asked. Its production descendants answer SQL under DP: smartnoise-sql, Uber's archived elastic-sensitivity rewriter, and Wilson et al.'s differentially private SQL, shipped today as BigQuery differential privacy. Two deliberate differences here. Those systems accept SQL and analyze or rewrite it, while this gateway never accepts SQL at all — the agent submits a small constrained AST, because a query language small enough to enumerate is a trust boundary small enough to test exhaustively. And every one of them puts a human analyst at the keyboard, where here the query author is an autonomous agent, and the threat model says so.

Natural-language database interfaces. Text-to-SQL is a large and successful field, but privacy is not its subject: the generated SQL runs with whatever authority the database grants. Where safety is addressed, as in SafeNLIDB (AAAI 2026), it is alignment-based — train the model to reason about what is safe to answer — so the guarantee lives inside the model. This project takes the complementary position: assume the model cannot be made safe, and enforce the guarantee below it with mathematics that holds even when the model is adversarial.

Agent and MCP privacy tooling. The emerging MCP-security stack addresses real risks — tool poisoning, prompt injection, exfiltration — with policy gateways, PII redaction and tokenization, and data-minimization patterns. Those controls govern what an agent can see and send. None of them bounds what a sequence of individually harmless answers cumulatively reveals, and that is the channel the attack gallery exploits. A differencing attack leaks a salary through two aggregates that a redaction proxy would happily pass. Differential privacy bounds exactly that channel, which makes it complementary to the rest of that stack rather than competition.

DP near LLMs, different problems. DP-SGD (e.g. Opacus) protects training examples inside model weights. DP in-context learning, DP synthetic text, and DP-RAG protect prompts and retrieval corpora. Local DP, as in Apple's and Google's telemetry, noises data on-device before it is ever collected. This project is the older, central-model setting those all descend from: a trusted curator, an untrusted questioner, and a budget between them.

The claim, stated carefully. There is no new differential-privacy mathematics in this repository. The contribution is the combination, and the evidence: an open, attack-validated artifact that puts agentic natural-language access in front of a DP aggregate backend under an explicit untrusted-model threat model. As far as I can find, no other open MCP server enforces differential privacy with a persisted budget beneath an untrusted agent. If you know of one, open an issue — I would genuinely like to compare notes.

Repository layout

.
├── README.md            ← you are here
├── DESIGN.md            ← architecture, threat model, the math, the budget design
├── SETUP.md             ← local setup, running the tests, configuration knobs
├── engine/              ← DP engine: mechanism, RNG, sensitivity, budget accountant + store
├── validation/          ← the trust boundary: policy checks, guards, and the repair loop
├── compiler/            ← the untrusted LLM NL→AST compiler
├── attacks/             ← the attack gallery: differencing, membership ε-sweep, patients singling-out
├── service/             ← AnalyticsService + audit log: the transport-agnostic core every surface shares
├── mcp_server/          ← the stdio MCP server: tool schemas generated from the dataset policy
├── datasets/            ← owner-authored dataset policies, ingestion, and the bundled patients demo
├── identity/            ← the identity layer the budget is keyed to
├── api/                 ← FastAPI service
├── ui/                  ← Streamlit front-end with the live budget meter
├── benchmarks/          ← manual latency benchmarks (run by hand, never by pytest)
├── docs/                ← the Claude Desktop walkthrough, the demo GIF, and the session chart assets
├── scripts/             ← fetch_data.py (pulls UCI Adult into data/, never committed) + the demo GIF renderer
└── tests/               ← unit, trust-boundary, privacy-guarantee, and attack regression tests (DESIGN.md section 8)

Author's note

This project is where I work through the design of privacy-preserving data systems and least-privilege data access in public: the trust boundary, the budget accounting, and the attack demos are the parts I'd defend in a design review.

Related work Where this sits among the existing tools, and what it deliberately does differently. DP libraries, DP query engines, text-to-SQL, MCP security tooling, and DP near LLMs (click to expand) DP libraries. OpenDP, Google's differential-privacy libraries, IBM's diffprivlib, and Tumult Analytics (which powered U.S. Census Bureau, Wikimedia, and IRS releases before its team joined LinkedIn in 2025 and the library moved into the OpenDP organization) are vetted implementations of the mechanisms themselves, written for a trusted analyst to call from their own code. This project hand-rolls its mechanism instead, so that every line of the privacy-critical path stays small, legible, and testable in one repo — and then cross-checks it against OpenDP, precisely because a hand-rolled mechanism means nothing without an external referee. For a real deployment the advice above stands: use a vetted library. DP query engines. PINQ (McSherry, 2009) established the architecture this project inherits: an untrusted analyst issues queries through a trusted layer that guarantees differential privacy no matter what is asked. Its production descendants answer SQL under DP: smartnoise-sql, Uber's archived elastic-sensitivity rewriter, and Wilson et al.'s differentially private SQL, shipped today as BigQuery differential privacy. Two deliberate differences here. Those systems accept SQL and analyze or rewrite it, while this gateway never accepts SQL at all — the agent submits a small constrained AST, because a query language small enough to enumerate is a trust boundary small enough to test exhaustively. And every one of them puts a human analyst at the keyboard, where here the query author is an autonomous agent, and the threat model says so. Natural-language database interfaces. Text-to-SQL is a large and successful field, but privacy is not its subject: the generated SQL runs with whatever authority the database grants. Where safety is addressed, as in SafeNLIDB (AAAI 2026), it is alignment-based — train the model to reason about what is safe to answer — so the guarantee lives inside the model. This project takes the complementary position: assume the model cannot be made safe, and enforce the guarantee below it with mathematics that holds even when the model is adversarial. Agent and MCP privacy tooling. The emerging MCP-security stack addresses real risks — tool poisoning, prompt injection, exfiltration — with policy gateways, PII redaction and tokenization, and data-minimization patterns. Those controls govern what an agent can see and send. None of them bounds what a sequence of individually harmless answers cumulatively reveals, and that is the channel the attack gallery exploits. A differencing attack leaks a salary through two aggregates that a redaction proxy would happily pass. Differential privacy bounds exactly that channel, which makes it complementary to the rest of that stack rather than competition. DP near LLMs, different problems. DP-SGD (e.g. Opacus) protects training examples inside model weights. DP in-context learning, DP synthetic text, and DP-RAG protect prompts and retrieval corpora. Local DP, as in Apple's and Google's telemetry, noises data on-device before it is ever collected. This project is the older, central-model setting those all descend from: a trusted curator, an untrusted questioner, and a budget between them. The claim, stated carefully. There is no new differential-privacy mathematics in this repository. The contribution is the combination, and the evidence: an open, attack-validated artifact that puts agentic natural-language access in front of a DP aggregate backend under an explicit untrusted-model threat model. As far as I can find, no other open MCP server enforces differential privacy with a persisted budget beneath an untrusted agent. If you know of one, open an issue — I would genuinely like to compare notes. blocks.html_en: Latanya Sweeney showed in 2002 that ZIP code + birth date + sex uniquely identify roughly 87% of Americans. You do not need someone's name to find them in a dataset; a few innocuous attributes will do. The gallery's third attack (attacks/patients_alice.py) reproduces that structure on 20 synthetic patients: sex and age alone narrow the cohort to exactly one person, Alice, the only woman over 64.

blocks.html_en: With privacy off, subtracting two perfectly ordinary demographic histograms recovers Alice's diagnosis exactly. No outlier value is required; being re-identifiable is enough, which makes this the strongest attack in the gallery. With privacy on, three independent defenses end it: the filter guard rejects the obvious narrow query outright (spending nothing); calibrated noise drowns the two-query subtraction (signal-to-noise ≈ 0.13, so the recovered "diagnosis" is essentially a random draw); and the budget refuses the averaging escalation long before it could work (~256 repetitions needed, 10 affordable). This is the attack the demo GIF at the top of this page, and the Claude Desktop walkthrough, replay live. Outcomes are regression-tested in tests/test_attack_patients.py.

blocks.html_en: Every answer is noised. An exact ledger of cumulative disclosure is kept per identity and persisted to disk, and the gateway refuses to answer before that ledger can exceed the guarantee it advertises. It never quietly degrades to a noisier answer instead.

blocks.html_en: DP libraries. OpenDP, Google's differential-privacy libraries, IBM's diffprivlib, and Tumult Analytics (which powered U.S. Census Bureau, Wikimedia, and IRS releases before its team joined LinkedIn in 2025 and the library moved into the OpenDP organization) are vetted implementations of the mechanisms themselves, written for a trusted analyst to call from their own code. This project hand-rolls its mechanism instead, so that every line of the privacy-critical path stays small, legible, and testable in one repo — and then cross-checks it against OpenDP, precisely because a hand-rolled mechanism means nothing without an external referee. For a real deployment the advice above stands: use a vetted library.

blocks.html_en: DP query engines. PINQ (McSherry, 2009) established the architecture this project inherits: an untrusted analyst issues queries through a trusted layer that guarantees differential privacy no matter what is asked. Its production descendants answer SQL under DP: smartnoise-sql, Uber's archived elastic-sensitivity rewriter, and Wilson et al.'s differentially private SQL, shipped today as BigQuery differential privacy. Two deliberate differences here. Those systems accept SQL and analyze or rewrite it, while this gateway never accepts SQL at all — the agent submits a small constrained AST, because a query language small enough to enumerate is a trust boundary small enough to test exhaustively. And every one of them puts a human analyst at the keyboard, where here the query author is an autonomous agent, and the threat model says so.

blocks.html_en: Natural-language database interfaces. Text-to-SQL is a large and successful field, but privacy is not its subject: the generated SQL runs with whatever authority the database grants. blocks.html_en: Agent and MCP privacy tooling. The emerging MCP-security stack addresses real risks — tool poisoning, prompt injection, exfiltration — with policy gateways, PII redaction and tokenization, and data-minimization patterns. Those controls govern what an agent can see and send. None of them bounds what a sequence of individually harmless answers cumulatively reveals, and that is the channel the attack gallery exploits. A differencing attack leaks a salary through two aggregates that a redaction proxy would happily pass. Differential privacy bounds exactly that channel, which makes it complementary to the rest of that stack rather than competition.

content_html_zh:
为人工智能代理提供对敏感数据的查询访问权限，并从数学上保证任何个人的记录都不会泄露——即使代理是错误的、被操纵的或敌对的。

录制的 Claude 桌面会话（回复经过修剪；图表卡是会话自己的）。 人工智能代理通过诊断对 20 名患者进行了分类，±12 的噪音淹没了每个垃圾箱。 提醒它无法关闭噪音，它会耗尽三个答案的预算，直到大门返回拒绝而不是更安静的答案。 在 32,561 行人口普查中，过于狭窄的部分在信任边界处被拒绝，而完整的教育细目则在规模上得到了清晰的结果。 拒绝和拒绝才是live gateway的真正执行，由python script/render_demo_gif.py重现。

一目了然

  • 工作攻击，而不是主张。 三种经典的隐私攻击——差异化、成员推理和重新识别挑出——针对系统自己的引擎运行。 每一个都在隐私关闭的情况下成功，在隐私开启的情况下失败，并固定在 CI 中，这样防御就不会悄然腐烂。
  • 独立验证的数学。 噪声机制是从头开始构建的，它与行业参考实现 OpenDP 相匹配，所有 35 项噪声等级检查均在 1e-9 以内。
  • 更严格的会计处理带来更多问题。 在部署的每个查询 ε 中，混合 zCDP 组合在相同预算下允许 308 个查询，而高级组合下为 268 个，朴素求和下为 100 个。 保证是 (ε, δ)-DP 而不是纯 ε。
  • 专为人工智能代理而构建。 作为 Claude Desktop 的 MCP 服务器运行。 连接代理在设计上是不受信任的，并且每个隐私属性都在其下方强制执行。
  • 堆栈：Python · DuckDB · FastAPI · Streamlit · MCP SDK · Docker · GitHub Actions，在 CI 中包含 250 多个测试套件。

您用简单的英语询问有关敏感数据集的问题。 法学硕士将每个问题编译成一个小的、受限的查询。 差分隐私引擎在跟踪的隐私预算下执行它，并返回具有规定置信区间的故意嘈杂的答案。 这个名字很合适。 与其同名的音频一样，该网关将每个信号保持在本底噪声下的设定阈值以下：任何个人的贡献都会被淹没，而人口规模的信号几乎不受影响地通过。 无论提出什么问题或措辞多么巧妙，都无法从答案中重建任何个人记录。

有趣的部分不是法学硕士可以编写查询。 而是隐私保证并不取决于法学硕士是否值得信赖。 该模型可以方便地提出查询。 它没有强制执行任何内容。 每个隐私属性都由下游组件强制执行，如果人类手动输入查询，这些组件的行为方式相同。 这是您应用于生产系统中任何不受信任的输入的信任边界规则，此处应用于人工智能代理。

标题：攻击画廊

任何人都可以主张隐私。 该存储库提供了会破坏声明的漏洞，针对其自己的引擎运行它们，并将结果固定在 CI 中。 了解网关所保证的内容的最快方法是观察它如何击败三种经典攻击，这些攻击会破坏简单的“查询数据库”系统。

攻击 1——差分攻击

差异攻击通过询问两个与某人完全不同的聚合问题来隔离该人。

Query A: "Total income of all 100 people in department X."        → $7,240,000
Query B: "Total income of all people in department X except Alice." → $7,135,000
Attacker computes: A − B = $105,000  ← Alice's exact salary, leaked.

这两个查询都是“只是聚合”。 两者都没有命名一行。 然而，它们一起暴露了一个人。 图库 (attacks/differencing.py) 显示此攻击在禁用隐私的情况下成功：目标的私有值被准确恢复。 （上面的薪资草图是说明性的；在真实的 UCI Adult 数据中，“Alice”是其所在团队最大资本收益的唯一持有者。） 然后，它显示一旦 DP 开启，相同的攻击就会被击败：每个答案上的校准噪声使得减法毫无用处，并且预算会计师对两个查询中发布的信息进行收费，而不是将它们视为独立的。

攻击 2——成员资格推断

成员资格推断攻击确定特定个体是否在数据集中。 对于许多数据集（医学研究、违约者名单）来说，这一事实本身就是敏感的。 仅具有查询访问权限的攻击者试图确定：“这就是数据中的具体人吗？”

该画廊在一系列隐私预算（ε——用答案准确性换取隐私的刻度盘）上运行了这种攻击，并绘制了结果：

最佳（内曼-皮尔逊）攻击者根据单个嘈杂的 COUNT 来确定一个人的成员资格，并在 ε 上与真实引擎运行。 经验成功（蓝色，95% 威尔逊区间）接近解析拉普拉斯曲线并保持在最坏情况 DP 上限（虚线）之下；随着 ε 的缩小，它从确定性（DP 关闭）向 0.5 次硬币翻转方向崩溃。 绿色效用曲线（右轴）显示了同一扫描中聚合查询的相对误差，在攻击失败的地方几乎没有凹陷。 由 python -m Attacks.membership 生成（每 ε 10,000 次试验）。

随着 ε 的缩小（隐私性更强），攻击者的成功就像抛硬币一样。 实用程序叠加显示了所付出的代价：击败单人攻击的相同噪音几乎无法移动人口规模的总量。 隐私不是免费的，图表准确地显示了您所交换的内容。 扫描范围 ε = 8 降至 0.5 以覆盖整个范围；捆绑部署对每个查询收取 ε = 0.05 的费用，超出了该图表的左边缘，其中单查询攻击已经与偶然攻击无法区分。

攻击3——通过重新识别挑出

Latanya Sweeney 在 2002 年表明，邮政编码 + 出生日期 + 性别可以唯一地识别大约 87% 的美国人。 您不需要某人的名字即可在数据集中找到他们；一些无害的属性就可以了。 该画廊的第三次攻击 (attacks/ Patients_alice.py) 在 20 名合成患者身上重现了这一结构：仅性别和年龄就将队列缩小到一个人，爱丽丝，唯一超过 64 岁的女性。

在隐私关闭的情况下，减去两个完全普通的人口统计直方图就可以准确地恢复爱丽丝的诊断。 不需要异常值；能够重新识别就足够了，这使得这是画廊中最强的攻击。 在启用隐私的情况下，三个独立的防御措施可以结束它：过滤器守卫直接拒绝明显的狭窄查询（不花任何钱）；校准噪声淹没了两个查询的减法（信噪比 ≈ 0.13，因此恢复的“诊断”本质上是随机抽取）；而且预算在平均升级发挥作用之前就拒绝了它（需要大约 256 次重复，10 次可以承受）。 这是本页顶部的攻击演示 GIF，以及克劳德桌面演练，现场重播。 结果在tests/test_attack_患者.py 中进行回归测试。

这些针对系统自身引擎运行的实验是核心证据，证明该保证是真实且可理解的，而不是从图书馆导入并被信仰所接受。

与 OpenDP 进行交叉检查

这些攻击验证了针对我们自己的数学的保证。 为了防止自洽但错误的实现，该机制还针对 OpenDP 作为独立参考进行交叉检查（attacks/crosscheck_opendp.py，opendp 0.15.1）。

简而言之：从头开始构建的机制与行业参考的小数点后九位一致，而故意错误校准的版本未能通过相同的测试，因此该协议具有一定的意义。 通过两种方式检查一致性：针对 OpenDP 认证范围的灵敏度和噪声标度，以及针对 OpenDP 的采样器的实际分布，并使用阳性对照证明测试可能会失败。 测量数据位于 DESIGN.md 第 6.3 节中。

OpenDP 是参考，而不是实现：它仅存在于 dev extras 中，运行的系统不会导入它。 规模协议在tests/test_crosscheck_opendp.py中进行回归测试（本地没有OpenDP的情况下会跳过；CI安装它并设置REQUIRE_OPENDP=1，因此检查永远不会默默地跳过那里）。

它是如何运作的

三个阶段。 只有第一个是不可信的，而这种不对称就是整个想法。

  Natural language question
            │
            ▼
  ┌───────────────────┐
  │   LLM compiler    │   Emits a CONSTRAINED QUERY AST (not free SQL),
  │   (UNTRUSTED)     │   via structured/schema-forced output.
  └───────────────────┘
            │  query AST
            ▼
  ┌───────────────────┐
  │  Validation /     │   Policy check: allowed columns only, aggregates
  │  guardrail layer  │   only, declared value ranges, group-cardinality
  │   (TRUSTED)       │   caps. Invalid → repair loop or refusal.
  └───────────────────┘
            │  validated AST
            ▼
  ┌───────────────────┐
  │  Privacy engine   │   Clamp to declared range (bounds sensitivity),
  │   (TRUSTED)       │   add calibrated Laplace noise, decrement budget.
  └───────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
  Noisy answer + confidence interval + remaining budget

最重要的设计选择是标记为“不可信”的盒子。 验证层之上的所有内容都被视为敌对的，而其下方的所有内容都是执行保证的可信计算基础。 LLM 编译为受约束的 AST 而不是任意 SQL，因为该约束限制了查询敏感度，而有界敏感度则使噪声校准听起来更可靠。 自由格式 SQL 将重新打开该项目关闭的攻击面。

隐私模型

每个答案都充满噪音。 每个身份都会保留累积披露的准确分类账，并持久保存到磁盘上，并且在该分类账超出其所宣传的保证之前，网关拒绝回答。 它永远不会安静地降级为更吵闹的答案。

成本也值得同样清楚地说明。 保证是(ε,δ)-差分隐私，其严格弱于纯ε-DP。 在概率最大为 δ 的情况下，允许 ε 界限失败。 δ 不是额外的噪声，而是失效质量，这就是为什么它是从数据集导出而不是硬编码的。

完整的推导——灵敏度、拉普拉斯机制、混合 zCDP 会计以及 δ 的来源——位于 DESIGN.md 第 3 节和第 5.4 节中。 这就是所有希腊字母所在的地方。

这个项目是什么，不是什么

它证明了不受信任的自然语言层可以位于敏感数据前面，而不会损害正式的隐私保证，并且该保证由工作攻击而不是断言支持。

它不是生产隐私产品，不是实际部署中经过审查的 DP 库的替代品，也不是声称 LLM 生成的查询可以在无人保护的情况下安全运行。 但事实并非如此，这正是可信层存在的原因。

MCP 服务器和 HTTP 演示都为拥有该机器的单个本地主体提供服务，该主体可以轮换纪元或删除预算文件以重新开始。 因此，“外部方烧毁预算且无法收回”属性是在机制中展示的，而不是针对远程对手强制执行的。 缩小这一差距需要身份验证 (OAuth) 和多租户拆分仍在路线图上。 噪声采样器还有一个已知的浮点侧通道（Mironov 2012，DESIGN.md 第 5.5 节中介绍）。 不要将任何表面指向真实的监管数据，或将其视为经过审查的 DP 库的替代品，不受信任的一方可以在其中进行身份验证。

捆绑的数据集是公共 UCI 成人/人口普查收入数据集，这是差分隐私文献中的标准基准，因此这里的攻击与 ε 结果可直接与已发表的作品进行比较。 它一开始就不包含私有数据，因此存储库可以安全地发布。 隐私机制被证明好像记录是敏感的。

相关工作

它在现有工具中的位置，以及它故意做的不同之处。

DP libraries, DP query engines, text-to-SQL, MCP security tooling, and DP near LLMs (click to expand)

DP 库。 OpenDP、Google 的差分隐私库、IBM 的 diffprivlib 和 Tumult Analytics（在其团队于 2025 年加入 LinkedIn 之前为美国人口普查局、维基媒体和 IRS 的发布提供支持，并且该库移入 OpenDP 组织）本身都是经过审查的机制实现，为值得信赖的分析师编写，以便从他们自己的代码中进行调用。 相反，该项目手动滚动其机制，以便隐私关键路径的每一行都在一个存储库中保持小、清晰且可测试，然后将其与 OpenDP 进行交叉检查，正是因为没有外部裁判，手动机制毫无意义。 对于真正的部署，上面的建议是：使用经过审查的库。

DP 查询引擎。 PINQ（McSherry，2009）建立了该项目继承的架构：不受信任的分析师通过受信任的层发出查询，无论提出什么问题，该层都保证差异隐私。 它的产品后代在 DP 下响应 SQL：smartnoise-sql，Uber 的存档弹性敏感度重写器，以及 Wilson 等人的差分隐私 SQL，今天作为 BigQuery 差分隐私发布。 这里有两个故意的差异。 这些系统接受 SQL 并分析或重写它，而此网关根本不接受 SQL — 代理提交一个小的受限 AST，因为小到足以枚举的查询语言是小到足以进行详尽测试的信任边界。 每一个都在键盘上放置了一名人类分析师，其中查询作者是一个自主代理，威胁模型也是如此。

自然语言数据库接口。 文本到 SQL 是一个庞大且成功的领域，但隐私不是它的主题：生成的 SQL 会以数据库授予的任何权限运行。 在解决安全问题的地方，如 SafeNLIDB (AAAI 2026) 中，它是基于对齐的——训练模型来推理什么是安全的答案——因此保证存在于模型内部。 该项目采取了补充立场：假设模型无法保证安全，并用即使模型是对抗性的数学也能保证其安全。

代理和 MCP 隐私工具。 新兴的 MCP 安全堆栈通过策略网关、PII 编辑和标记化以及数据最小化模式来解决真正的风险——工具中毒、提示注入、渗漏。 这些控件控制代理可以看到和发送的内容。 它们都没有限制一系列单独无害的答案累积揭示的内容，而这正是攻击库所利用的渠道。 差异攻击通过两个聚合泄露了工资，编辑代理很乐意通过这两个聚合。 差异化隐私恰好限制了该渠道，这使得它与该堆栈的其余部分互补而不是竞争。

法学硕士附近的DP，不同的问题。 DP-SGD（例如 Opacus）保护模型权重内的训练示例。 DP 上下文学习、DP 合成文本和 DP-RAG 保护提示和检索语料库。 本地 DP，如苹果和谷歌的遥测技术，在收集数据之前就在设备上发出噪音。 这个项目是较旧的、中心模型设置，所有这些都源自：一个值得信赖的策展人，一个不值得信任的提问者，以及他们之间的预算。

该主张，陈述得很仔细。 该存储库中没有新的差分隐私数学。 贡献在于组合和证据：一个开放的、经过攻击验证的工件，它将代理自然语言访问置于显式不可信模型威胁模型下的 DP 聚合后端前面。 据我所知，没有其他开放 MCP 服务器可以在不受信任的代理下通过持续的预算来强制执行差异隐私。 如果你知道，请提出一个问题——我真的很想交换意见。

存储库布局

.
├── README.md            ← you are here
├── DESIGN.md            ← architecture, threat model, the math, the budget design
├── SETUP.md             ← local setup, running the tests, configuration knobs
├── engine/              ← DP engine: mechanism, RNG, sensitivity, budget accountant + store
├── validation/          ← the trust boundary: policy checks, guards, and the repair loop
├── compiler/            ← the untrusted LLM NL→AST compiler
├── attacks/             ← the attack gallery: differencing, membership ε-sweep, patients singling-out
├── service/             ← AnalyticsService + audit log: the transport-agnostic core every surface shares
├── mcp_server/          ← the stdio MCP server: tool schemas generated from the dataset policy
├── datasets/            ← owner-authored dataset policies, ingestion, and the bundled patients demo
├── identity/            ← the identity layer the budget is keyed to
├── api/                 ← FastAPI service
├── ui/                  ← Streamlit front-end with the live budget meter
├── benchmarks/          ← manual latency benchmarks (run by hand, never by pytest)
├── docs/                ← the Claude Desktop walkthrough, the demo GIF, and the session chart assets
├── scripts/             ← fetch_data.py (pulls UCI Adult into data/, never committed) + the demo GIF renderer
└── tests/               ← unit, trust-boundary, privacy-guarantee, and attack regression tests (DESIGN.md section 8)
